en.headline: Lee says government will study paying some mainland deals in yuan
en.dek: On radio, the chief executive said Hong Kong already handles most offshore yuan trades and should push the currency further into bonds, contracts and training fees.
body: Chief Executive John Lee said on Friday the government would study using the yuan for some contracts and transactions with the mainland, including paying part of the cost when civil servants attend training at mainland institutions.

Speaking on an RTHK English-programme interview about the first five-year plan, Lee said about 75 to 85 per cent of offshore yuan transactions already take place in Hong Kong, but the city could do more to promote the currency's international use. He cited allowing investors to buy bonds in yuan as one example. The five-year plan calls for strengthening Hong Kong's role as a global offshore yuan business hub.

Lee also discussed talent and artificial intelligence. He said various talent admission schemes had brought more than 300,000 people to Hong Kong, about 20 per cent of them from outside the mainland, and that more than half of those admitted were willing to stay. He said the government still needed to work on retention.

On AI, he said the public had to understand the risks as the technology became more widely used. He said he was concerned that young people who became overly absorbed in AI worlds might withdraw from family and classmates, or treat an AI system as their only friend.

zh.headline: 李家超：研究與內地部分合約或交易用人民幣
zh.dek: 特首在電台表示，香港已處理大部分離岸人民幣交易，下一步可把人民幣用到債券、合約及培訓開支。
body: 行政長官李家超周五表示，政府會研究與內地的部分合約或交易使用人民幣，例如公務員到內地機構培訓時，研究以人民幣繳付部分款項。
李家超在港台英語節目談及首份五年規劃時說，現時約75%至85%離岸人民幣交易在香港進行，但認為可以做得更好，推動人民幣國際化，例如容許投資者以人民幣購買債券。五年規劃提出強化香港作為全球離岸人民幣業務樞紐的功能。
人才方面，他說各項人才入境計劃已吸引超過30萬人來港，當中約兩成來自內地以外地方，目前超過一半願意繼續留港，但當局仍需努力挽留人才。
談到人工智能，李家超說在普及應用的同時，必須讓公眾了解潛在風險。他關注年輕人若過度沉迷人工智能世界，可能減少與家人或同學交流，甚至把人工智能視為唯一朋友。
